items.title: Containers/image: digest type does not guarantee valid type
items.summary: A flaw was found in the github.com/containers/image library. This flaw allows attackers to trigger unexpected authenticated registry accesses on behalf of a victim user, causing resource exhaustion, local path traversal, and other attacks.

items.title: Themify Base <= 1.2.4 - Subscriber+ Privilege Escalation
items.summary: Themify Base WordPress theme through 1.2.4 does not perform capability checks on its option save and read AJAX actions, which are protected only by a generic nonce that other commonly expose on the front end, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to update arbitrary blog options such as the default role and open registration, and gain administrator access when such a is active.

items.title: Popup Builder <= 4.4.6 - Admin+ SSRF via sgpb-background-image
items.summary: The Popup Builder WordPress plugin through 4.4.6 does not validate a user-supplied URL before requesting it server-side and storing the fetched response so that it can be read back, allowing users with Administrator privileges to perform Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks and read the responses of internal services.

items.title: Popup Builder <= 4.4.6 - Authenticated Private and Draft Post Content Disclosure via Popup Preview
items.summary: The Popup Builder WordPress plugin through 4.4.6 does not properly check authorization before allowing a user to store popup preview data against arbitrary posts, nor restrict who can read that content back on public requests, allowing users granted access to the Popup Builder WordPress plugin through 4.4.6 to disclose the private and draft content of posts they do not own to unauthenticated visitors.

items.title: Popup Builder <= 4.4.6 - Unauthenticated Draft and Private Popup Content Disclosure via 'sg popup id' Parameter
items.summary: The Popup Builder WordPress plugin through 4.4.6 does not check the publish status or the visitor's capabilities before rendering a popup requested by its ID in the URL, allowing unauthenticated users to read the content and configuration of popups that are still drafts or are marked private.
